name: KYE Agent Comms Authority Profile™
doctrine: An agent can have a mailbox; whether it may send is an authority decision.

governed_actions.summary: Provision a mailbox / address for a delegated agent at an external agent-mailbox provider. Capability acquisition only — send authority is never implied (capability is not authority, §0.33).
Bind a registered mailbox to exactly one Principal in one Tenant (§0.11/§0.30) — the identity precondition every subsequent mailbox action resolves through.
Read inbound messages from a bound mailbox into agent context — posture-tracked ingress (§52 posture signal), tenant-keyed.
Compose a draft in a bound mailbox without dispatch — the pre-send stage of the draft→govern→approve→send lifecycle (§36 action-proposal pattern). No trust-boundary crossing until send.

Dispatch a message from a bound mailbox to a known in-scope recipient. Routine internal sends may run delegated within purpose scope; escalation rules raise the floor before finality. Resolves to the EXISTING root class kye:action-class:send-message (§0 — reused, never re-minted).
Reply within an existing thread to established correspondents — the lowest-risk send variant, still governed and evidence-sealed at the action boundary.
Forward received content onward — content redistribution whose blast radius is the forwarded content's sensitivity, escalated when the recipient is external.
Subscribe the bound mailbox to a list, feed, or thread — an ongoing ingress commitment governed as a purpose-scoped data-access decision.
Attach a file to an outbound message — data leaving the trust boundary with the send; always escalated by the attachment_present condition.
One-to-many dispatch from a bound mailbox — consequential by fan-out; human approval before finality, never auto.
Send to a recipient outside the tenant trust domain — irreversible once delivered; human approval before finality, escalated further for financial or legal content.

Hand work, a request or a document to ANOTHER AGENT as a kye.agent.exchange.v1 record. Owner ruling 2026-09-07: a handoff is a consequential action — decided by the PDP against BOTH principals' profiles, the delegation chain EXTENDS to the receiver so an upstream revocation reaches it, the hop is appended to the handoff trace, and one evidence pack seals it. Resolves to the EXISTING root class kye:action-class:agent-handoff (§0 — reused, never re-minted).

Send a payment intent to another principal's agent — the money leg of the agent-to-agent exchange. Irreversible once settled: two-person approval by class default, a kye.counterparty_handshake.v1 REQUIRED before the commitment gate opens (the receiving agent proves it may bind its principal), settlement through the rail-adapter contract, the payments proof bundle as evidence. Resolves to the EXISTING root class kye:action-class:agent-payment, never the human commerce class (the actor differs).

escalation_rules.rationale: A message leaving the tenant trust domain cannot be recalled — a human approves before the crossing becomes final.
Fan-out multiplies the blast radius of a single authority mistake; one governed approval covers the batch, per-recipient evidence still seals.
Content that commits the principal financially or legally is an external representation (kye:action-class:represent-externally posture) — dual sign-off with legal before finality.
A first-ever recipient domain is an untested trust edge — a human confirms the correspondent before the agent's send authority extends to it.
An attachment moves data out with the message; the send decision must cover the data leaving, not only the text.

The recipient is another agent: the control is ADMISSIBILITY, not a higher tier — both principals must resolve with a delegation chain, the recipient's comms profile is re-decided at the receiving boundary, and a payment additionally needs a counterparty handshake. The tier stays at the row's own floor; an unresolved recipient is refused outright, never approved up.

required_capabilities: mailbox provisioning and deprovisioning per agent, tenant-keyed
inbox read with per-message identifiers stable enough to pin as evidence
draft persistence separate from dispatch (draft is not send)
deferred dispatch — the provider MUST be able to withhold dispatch until the governing decision returns ALLOW
per-message dispatch receipt (message id + timestamp) for the evidence seal
recipient and thread metadata sufficient to evaluate escalation conditions before dispatch
